content:
Rafael Mendes: heads up: perf canary alerts are *way* too noisy since we turned on the FP8/INT8 cohorts yesterday. got paged 3x overnight for TTFT p95 “regression” that disappeared on rerun. we need to tune baselines / noise suppression before we expand regions.

Allison Grant: yeah seeing it too. the current rule is comparing 15m window canary vs baseline with no min sample size, so a couple long prompts will blow it up.

Allison Grant: grafana panel where it’s most obvious: https://grafana.redwoodinference.net/d/perf-canary/fp8-int8-rollout?var-region=us-east&var-model=all&var-mode=fp8

GrafanaBot: Alert triggered: perf-canary-ttft-p95-regression
Labels: region=us-east model=llama-3-70b mode=fp8 gpu=h100
Value: +14.8% over baseline (threshold 8%)

Rafael Mendes: ^ this one. when i drilled in, canary sample was like 38 requests total.

Noah Patel: +1. if we don’t gate on sample size and distribution stability, p95 is basically random. we should require N>= (say) 300 requests / 10k tokens or something per slice.

Julian Moore: also note: our canary jobs are missing a bunch of tags. i can’t consistently split by kernel_mode vs scheduler config. some of the “regressions” are likely mixed cohorts.

Sofia Ivanova: scheduler side: we changed batching window defaults in canary (mixed workload tuning). could be interacting with the alert math, because the baseline window includes both old+new scheduler when cohort assignment is leaky.

Grace Kim: kernel side: some models are using fallback kernels on certain shapes. if the alert doesn’t break down by `kernel_variant`, you’ll see weird averages.

Allison Grant: ok, concretely, current alert rules:
- ttft_p95_regression: (canary_p95 - baseline_p95) / baseline_p95 > 0.08 for 2 consecutive evals (eval=15m)
- tpot_p95_regression: same but > 0.10
- tokens_s_p50_drop: (baseline - canary)/baseline > 0.07
No minimum sample size and baseline is “last 24h” by region+model only.

Rafael Mendes: propose:
1) add min sample size per alert eval (both baseline and canary)
2) baseline should be per GPU SKU + model + route type (chat vs completions) at minimum
3) add tags for `kernel_mode` (fp8/int8/bf16), `kernel_variant`, and `scheduler_profile`

Julian Moore: for (3), we already have a PR in flight to tag scheduler metrics with model/gpu/kernel-mode. i can extend to include scheduler profile. but kernel_variant might need runtime registry to expose.

Grace Kim: kernel_variant tagging is doable. for the immediate sprint, we can at least tag `kernel_dispatch` as {fp8_attn,int8_gemm,baseline}. more granular variants might be too cardinality-heavy.

Allison Grant: careful on cardinality. if kernel_variant includes shapes we’ll explode metrics. but a coarse dispatch bucket is fine.

Noah Patel: +1. we need debug-ability without turning metrics into a DoS.

Irene Choi: also confirming there was driver drift on one of the us-east canary clusters (A100 pool got a different image). could be impacting variance. we’re fixing but alerts should not page on that type of churn.

Rafael Mendes: yep. we should make these alerts “ticket” severity unless confirmed with enough sample. paging is too aggressive.

Allison Grant: we can:
- switch to multi-window, multi-burn style: require 2/3 windows (15m, 1h) breach AND N>=min
- add “soft alert” slack notification for early signal, but only page if sustained.

Sahana Iyer: from CI/perf gate perspective, we already do noise suppression via EWMA and minimum run count. can we borrow the same logic for canary? i can help port.

Allison Grant: yes pls. can you share the thresholds you used + how you handled outliers?

Sahana Iyer: roughly: ignore top/bottom 1% of latencies, compute p95 on remaining, require >= 500 samples, then EWMA over 6 evals. (it’s imperfect but way less noisy)

Noah Patel: i’m a little nervous about trimming in prod canary because outliers might be real. but we can do min sample + longer window first. trimming might hide issues.

Rafael Mendes: agree. let’s start conservative:
- min N
- longer evaluation window(s)
- baseline pinned per gpu/model/mode
- page only if sustained

Allison Grant: baseline pinned per gpu/model/mode requires us to actually have those labels on the baseline metrics too. currently baseline series doesn’t include mode because it’s “all traffic” for the model.

Julian Moore: that’s the metric tagging gap. if the baseline mixes bf16 + fp8 fallback traffic, it’s apples/oranges. we need `kernel_mode` tag everywhere.

Grace Kim: ok i’ll coordinate with Yuki on runtime side: ensure `kernel_mode` is emitted as a tag on request metrics. (there’s already an internal flag `--kernel_mode_override`; we can map to tag)

Rafael Mendes: can we have something in place today to stop paging? even a blunt min sample would help.

Allison Grant: i can hot-edit the alert rule now:
- add `sum(rate(requests_total[15m])) > 200` as a condition
- switch paging contact point to slack only for the next 24h
- keep incident paging only on error rate + hard SLO breaches

Rafael Mendes: do it. please drop the diff here once applied.

Allison Grant: applied:
- ttft_p95_regression: now requires canary_requests_15m >= 200 AND baseline_requests_15m >= 200
- increased eval window for page from 15m->30m
- routing to #eng-sre-alerts (no pager) for this alert family until we re-baseline

GrafanaBot: Alert rule updated: perf-canary-ttft-p95-regression (contact point changed)

Irene Choi: on fleet side, we’ll also lock clocks on the canary nodes. we saw a couple nodes oscillating due to shared tenancy. shouldn’t happen in dedicated canary, but our pool isn’t perfectly isolated.

Noah Patel: baseline: do we want “last 7d median” rather than last 24h mean? 24h includes the ongoing rollout turbulence.

Allison Grant: yep. i can set baseline to “previous stable cohort” by label if we have it, otherwise fallback to 7d. but we need `cohort=baseline` vs `cohort=canary` consistent.

Rafael Mendes: we *do* have cohort labels on perf-canary service. but the runtime metrics that feed TTFT are missing it for some codepaths.

Julian Moore: that’s on me; scheduler metrics PR added tags, but request latency histograms come from gateway layer. different pipeline.

Grace Kim: we can at least tag at gateway: model, route, region, gpu, kernel_mode, cohort. kernel dispatch happens in runtime, but mode is set via config at deployment.

Allison Grant: action items:
1) (Today) keep alert family non-paging + min sample + longer window (done)
2) (This week) add required tags: model,gpu,region,cohort,kernel_mode,route_type (Julian/Grace)
3) (This week) update baseline logic to compare canary vs baseline cohort per tag set (Allison)
4) define “debug dimensions” we require for rollout: kernel_dispatch_bucket + scheduler_profile (Grace/Julian)

Rafael Mendes: + add explicit “small sample false positive” note in runbook. we’ll keep getting questions.

Allison Grant: added to runbook draft, will link once merged.

Sofia Ivanova: re scheduler_profile: we have 3 presets right now (mixed-low-latency, mixed-throughput, decode-heavy). i’ll make sure those are discrete strings and not config hashes.

Noah Patel: please avoid config hash tags, we’ll end up with infinite time series.

Rafael Mendes: thanks all. once tags land + baseline is stable, we can re-enable paging for sustained regressions only. for now, keep canary small (us-east only) until the signal is trustworthy.

Allison Grant: ack. i’ll post an update in #eng-runtime too so they don’t panic when alerts stop paging.

Rafael Mendes: :thumbsup: also please add a panel that overlays sample size next to p95 deltas. would’ve saved me 30 min last night.

Allison Grant: on it. adding “req count” + “token count” panels adjacent to TTFT/TPOT deltas.
